title: Every Black-Footed Ferret Alive Descends From Just 7 Animals
subject: black-footed ferret

scenes.text: Every animal of this species alive today comes from just seven ancestors.
The black-footed ferret nearly vanished. A last small group turned up on a Wyoming ranch in 1981.
Only eighteen were caught to start a breeding program. Only seven of them ever had young.
About 650 are alive today, and every one is a relative of those seven.
In December 2020, scientists cloned one from tissue frozen in the nineteen eighties. Her name is Elizabeth Ann.
A ferret born forty years late, to give a whole species more family.

description:
All living black-footed ferrets descend from just seven animals that bred in captivity.
In 2020, scientists cloned a ferret from tissue frozen in the 1980s.
Should we clone more endangered animals?
first_comment: Elizabeth Ann was cloned from a female named Willa, who died in the mid-1980s. Should cloning be used to save more endangered species?
